input.question: How can I go to sleep extremely hungry/thirsty yet wake up and not feel the hunger/thirst at all?
input.ground_truth: After the energy of the food you consumed is used up, your blood sugar drops and the body enters a fasting state. The liver releases small doses of glucose by breaking down glycogen to maintain your blood sugar (in your case while sleeping). So when you wake up your blood sugar is at the right level and you don't feel hungry.

Okay! Imagine you are really, really hungry or thirsty before you go to bed. Maybe you didn’t have a snack or drink any water.

But when you sleep, your brain kind of takes a little nap too. So, you don’t notice the hunger or thirst as much while you’re sleeping.

When you wake up, your body feels better because:

1. While you were sleeping, your body was resting and using up less energy.
2. Sometimes, your body uses a little bit of its stored energy (like saved-up food and water) while you sleep.
3. When you wake up, you might not feel as hungry or thirsty right away because your body is just waking up and it takes a few minutes to remember it was hungry or thirsty.

But if you stay hungry or thirsty for a long time, it’s not good for your body. It’s better to have something to eat or drink when you can!
